title: A2C agent output (a2c-structure-transcriber)
description: One drawn CHEMICAL STRUCTURE, read into machine-readable notation. Item = one A2 figure/equation block whose artwork is a structural formula or a reaction scheme. This is a transcription, not a rendering decision: the exports keep showing NCERT's own drawing, because an RDKit depiction is a standard drawing and would match the book less. What SMILES buys is the other half of this project -- a question's structure can be matched against a chapter's by substructure rather than by words. Reading a drawn ring into SMILES is a judgement about a picture, which is why it is an agent step and not a script.

kind.description: `structure` = one or more discrete species drawn; `reaction` = reactants/products joined by an arrow; `not_a_structure` = the block is a photograph, a graph, an orbital diagram or anything else that has no SMILES. Choosing `not_a_structure` is a correct and expected answer, never a failure.

species.description: structure only: every discrete species drawn in the block, in reading order.

smiles.description: SMILES for this species, as drawn. Do not normalise, re-aromatise or 'correct' what the book draws.

label.description: The name printed beside it in the book, copied exactly, e.g. 'Aniline'. Empty if none is printed.

reaction_smiles.description: reaction only: reactants>agents>products. Agents (the reagent written over the arrow) go in the middle field, not with the reactants.

confidence.description: `unsure` is the honest answer for a structure drawn with an implicit or ambiguous group, and is preferred to a confident guess -- a wrong SMILES is worse than a missing one, because it will silently mis-match questions.

note.description: What was read and anything that constrained it: an R group left unspecified, a bond whose stereochemistry the drawing does not fix, a species drawn only as a label. Required.
